page: Amazon Web Services r7i.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 vCPUs and 96 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing Intel Xeon 8488C processors running at 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The instance achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Passmark CPU scores, and uncached memory bandwidth read and write operations. Single-core performance is moderate, placing in the middle 50% for stress-ng single-core tests and the top 25% for Geekbench single-core metrics. Cryptographic and vector instruction capabilities are supported by hardware flags including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to top-tier scores in Passmark encryption and ray tracing benchmarks.

Given the high memory density and multi-core capabilities, this instance is configured for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale database operations, in-memory caching, and data-intensive processing. Redis SET operations perform in the top 10%, and LLM inference benchmarks for medium and large models show strong performance in prompt processing and text generation. The lack of local storage requires external storage provisioning, which represents a structural tradeoff for I/O-heavy workloads that cannot fit entirely in the 1536.0 GB DDR5 memory space.
